newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Clariant still looking for acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Clariant still looking for acquisition.

text.p: Swiss chemicals maker Clariant AG, which was spun off from Sandoz AG in July 1995, is still looking for an acquisition to round out its business, Clariant chairman Rolf Schweizer said.
"We want to build additional pillars to make us less dependent on cyclical businesses like textiles," Schweizer told reporters following a speech to businessmen in Zurich.

He said the company was not currently in any acquisition negotiations, but Clariant was in the market for an acquisition or acquisitions worth a total of between some 500 million and 700 million Swiss francs.
Schweizer said the group would also look to round out its business.
He said Clariant was also looking to expand its "mass", or size in terms of turnover, in order to make mobility and the exchange of businesses easier.
No timetable has been set, but Schweizer said the company hoped it would be able to take the first steps toward these goals by the end of this year.
He further stated that Clariant still expected to meet its goals this year for a substantial improvement in net earnings and for sales growth above the market average.
Clariant reported 1995 group net income of 106 million francs. Its 1995 group sales totalled 2.145 billion francs. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
